In AnkiDroid, export a deck (.apkg) or your collection (.colpkg) with \"Include media\" checked, then import it here. Its cards count as the language you study, so import each language\'s deck while that language is selected. Only sentence audio is kept. Re-import after adding cards.

Pick a video or audio file, then its subtitles in the language you study (.srt, .vtt or .ass). Each subtitle line becomes one sentence, in order. Choose it from the menu at the top of the practice screen.
Downloads only the subtitles in the language you study.
Also downloads subtitles in this language (or in English, if a video has none), YouTube\'s machine translations included, and shows them as each line\'s translation.

No word field is set, so your cards\' words don\'t count as known.
n+0 plays only sentences where you know every word. n+1 to n+5 also let in sentences with up to that many words you don\'t know yet: more sentences, and new words to pick up by ear.
Kiku, Lapis and Senren are Japanese note types. Other languages use Anki Miner Note.
Imports keep only the audio from each preset\'s audio field. If you change the audio field, re-import your decks.
Sentences cooling down after Crystal Clear: %1$d
Every sentence you marked Crystal Clear comes back into practice now instead of after 10 days.
Cool-downs reset. All Crystal Clear sentences are back in practice.
Every blacklisted sentence comes back into practice.
Version %1$s. New versions are downloaded from GitHub Releases.
Check for updates when the app starts
You have %1$s. Updating keeps your imports and progress.
Android will first ask you to allow this app to install updates; allow it, come back and tap Update again.
the downloaded file is damaged (checksum mismatch)
Words you marked in sentences. Known ones count as known and are exported with your word list; ignored ones (names, sounds) only stop counting as unknown.
No words yet. Show a sentence\'s text and tap a word to mark it.
The export has your word list, your cards\' words and the words you marked known, one per line, ready for Jiten or Migaku.
Yomitan dictionaries for looking up words: show a sentence\'s text and tap a word.
Train your ear with sentences made of words you already know: from your Anki cards, your videos and YouTube. Each sentence loops until you understand it, and the text stays hidden until you want it.
Decks, videos, word lists and dictionaries are kept per language, so you can switch any time.
With dictionaries you can tap any word in a sentence to look it up, and mark it known or ignored. These are the dictionaries Hachidori installs by default; they update themselves.
Installing goes on in the background, so you can continue right away.
There are no ready-made dictionaries for %1$s yet. You can import any Yomitan dictionary later under Settings → Dictionaries.
The app plays only sentences made of words you know. Import your known words (from Jiten, Anki Miner or Migaku) and your Anki deck; you can also do it later in Settings.
Videos with subtitles and YouTube links are added under Settings → Videos and audio.
Press play and listen. The sentence repeats until you tap Crystal Clear, or by itself after the number of plays you choose.
Tap the card to show the text, then tap a word to look it up and mark it known or ignored.
The back arrow takes you to the sentence before and undoes what you did to it.
For hands-free listening, set auto advance to Crystal Clear or Skip after a few plays.
With headphones: tap to play or pause, double-tap to skip. The notification has the same buttons.
Dictionaries made from Wiktionary, for every language you can study. They update themselves.
Couldn\'t load the list of Wiktionary dictionaries. Check your connection.
Lookups show your dictionaries in this order; move them with the arrows.
With a dictionary you can tap any word in a sentence to look it up, and mark it known or ignored. Wiktionary has one for every language: choose the language of the definitions. It updates itself.
